title: Check your understanding: Preventing and Reviewing Merge Problems

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of preventing and reviewing merge problems?
options: Good merge hygiene includes reviewing the final diff, resolving conflicts intentionally, updating from the correct base and running project checks. Integration is not complete just because Git accepted the merge.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Good merge hygiene includes reviewing the final diff, resolving conflicts intentionally, updating from the correct base and running project checks. Integration is not complete just because Git accepted the merge.
questions.explanation: Good merge hygiene includes reviewing the final diff, resolving conflicts intentionally, updating from the correct base and running project checks. Integration is not complete just because Git accepted the merge.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git diff --check` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with preventing and reviewing merge problems?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
